main_text.p: neis, Macynia, Molycria, Chalcis,Nau-paƈtum , Pylene , Halifarma : quamvis ex his Molycriam & Naupaƈtum prior ætas ante Macedonum res auƈtas Locris Ozolis rectius accensuerit. Cætera verò regionis in vicos majores & minores nullis munitionibus tutos sparsa. Gentem Ætolorum universam bellicosam fuisse , corporibus validam , animis ferocem , turbidam , insolentem , superbam, cæteroqui libertatis confervandæ & armis tuendæ studiosam , scriptores veteres omnes tradiderunt. Satisque constat , perantiquam eorum libertatem fuisse, nullis regibus aut dominis obnoxiam, sed utplurimum populos & civitates Ætolici nominis seorsim sibi consuluisse,& respublicas quasdam suas peculiares habuisse, interdum etiam dissensionibus laborasse, & armis in se esse versos : urgente autem hoste externo sese conjunxisse,&communem patriam ac libertatem defendisse : cum finitimis , maximè autem cum Acarnanibus frequenter bella gessisse,& ob eos armis iam ab Atheniensibus esse petitos. Posteris verò temporibus , cum Macedonēs[?] à morte Alexandri Magni Græ-rum libertati vim facerent, & Græci Partes scissi essent , Ætoli omnes [illegible, ~2 letters]mplo Achæorum, quò rectius sibi confu-

page.notes: The page has one text column with no printed page number, running head or catchword. The text is one paragraph that continues from the previous page, so it has cont="true" and no internal paragraph breaks. Line-end hyphens are kept (Nau-, Græ-, confu-). The reading "Macedonēs[?]" is uncertain: the word is cut by a mark at the line start. "[illegible, ~2 letters]mplo" is also uncertain: the start of the word is hidden by a reference mark or show-through. The first word of the line after "Græ-" is partly hidden by show-through, so "rum" and "Partes" are read from the visible letters. The left edge carries cropped fragments of a margin column, none legible enough to transcribe as notes. The faint line at the foot is illegible and is marked as such; the foot line's word counts are estimates. Spelling was normalised for long s and for u/v and i/j as the rules require, so the ff of the scan is read as ss (fuisse, gessisse, consuluisse). The ligature ƈ (ct) in Naupaƈtum is kept as printed.
